*Generated by build_pointwise_report.py; competing pre-registered predictions P-a (target-blind splitting) vs P-b (variance seeking) in HYPOTHESIS.md ('Round 6'). mmd rows are round-2 results reused. Either outcome supports the paper claim that a scalar target does not determine the answer.*

## Initialization analysis (post-hoc, boss)

x_T ~ N(0,1) sits between the basins (modes at ±2). Reproducing each restart's init
(torch.manual_seed(seed+restart); randn) and crossing init side with final basin:

| arm | init side predicts basin | reading |
|---|---|---|
| (y−0)² | 51% (= chance; 78/80 land uni from BOTH sides) | pull to the low-variance basin overrides init entirely |
| (y−2)² | 68% | init matters at the margin: 19 of the 23 bi-landings started left |
| \|y−2\| | 74% | weakest objective → most init-driven (closest to prior-following) |

So the 29% bi-landings of (y−2)² are mostly runs that started on the bimodal side and
were not pulled out; the variance-seeking force dominates init for the squared losses.
